To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) VLCS activity is not required for VLCFA beta-oxdation, (2), VLCS activity is required to maintain normal plasma and tissue VLCFA levels and (3), VLCS is not required for peroxisomal beta-oxidation of VLCFA in the XAL mouse.
the Vlcs knockout and XALD/VLCS double knockout mouse models of X-ALDC have the same biochemical defects as X-ALD patients but do not have the same severe neurological and endocrine phenotypes.

(1) VLCS is the only VLCS in the mouse, (2) the XALD/VLCS double knockout mouse has biochemical characteristics similar to those seen in X-ALD but does not exhibit a more severe phenotype and (3) there is no direct interaction of VLCS with ABCD1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular basis of X-ALDS and other peroxisomal disorders.
understanding how the ABCD1 gene product, which is a peroxisome membrane protein with a predicted 6-transmembrane domain, is involved in the transport of fatty acids into peroxisome.
understanding the role of VLCS in peroxisomal beta-oxidation and the role of ABCD1 in the transport of VLCS to the peroxisomal lumen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
VLCS is the rate limiting enzyme in the peroxisomal beta-oxidation of VLCFA.
the Vlcs knockout does not mimic X-ALD.
the Vlcs mouse is a model for X-ALD and that the biochemical abnormalities observed are not responsible for the neurodegenerative disease observed in X-ALD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the XALD/VLCS double knockout mouse is a very long-chain acy-CoA synthetases deficient mouse and not an X-linked adrenoluekodystrophy mouse.
the Vlcs knockout is a very long chain acyl-CoA deficient mouse and that the Vlacs knockout is a very-long chain acyl-CoAsynthetase deficient mouse.
the biochemical signature of X-linked adrenomyeloneuropathy and X-linked adrenolukodystrophy is the result of decreased peroxisome biogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biochemical phenotype of X-ALDs is not a consequence of a decrease in VLCS activity but rather a consequence of the absence of the ABCD1 protein itself.
peroxisomal beta-oxidation of VLCFA is not required for normal health and survival.
the biochemical abnormalities observed are not sufficient to explain the severe neurological phenotype observed in X-ALD.
